english: Let $A=\{1,2,3\}$. For a relation $R$ on $A$, let $m(R)$ denote the least number of ordered pairs from $A\times A$ that must be added to $R$ so that the resulting relation is an equivalence relation on $A$. Then the arithmetic mean of $m(R)$, taken over all symmetric relations $R$ on $A$, is ______.
hindi: माना $A=\{1,2,3\}$ है। $A$ पर किसी संबंध $R$ के लिए माना $m(R)$, $A\times A$ के उन क्रमित युग्मों की न्यूनतम संख्या है जिन्हें $R$ में जोड़ने पर प्राप्त संबंध $A$ पर एक तुल्यता संबंध हो जाए। तब $A$ पर सभी सममित संबंधों $R$ पर लिया गया $m(R)$ का समांतर माध्य ______ है।
solution: A symmetric $R$ is fixed by its diagonal pairs ($2^{3}$ choices) and its set $E$ of unordered pairs $\{a,b\},\ a\neq b$ ($2^{3}$ choices): $2^{6}=64$ relations
The smallest equivalence relation containing $R$ has as classes the groups of elements linked through $E$; its size is the sum of squares of class sizes
$E$ empty: $3$; one pair: $2^{2}+1=5$; two or three pairs (all linked): $3^{2}=9$, so mean size $=\dfrac{3+3\cdot5+4\cdot9}{8}=6.75$
Mean of $n(R)$: each diagonal pair is in half the relations, each unordered pair brings $2$ ordered pairs in half: $\frac32+\frac{6}{2}=4.5$
$m(R)=$ (size of the smallest equivalence relation containing $R$) $-\,n(R)$, so the mean of $m(R)$ is $6.75-4.5=2.25$
solution_full: A symmetric relation on $A$ is determined by which of the $3$ diagonal pairs it contains and by which of the $3$ unordered pairs $\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}$ it contains (each contributing both ordered pairs). So there are $2^{3}\cdot2^{3}=64$ symmetric relations.

Any equivalence relation containing $R$ contains the diagonal and, by transitivity, all pairs of elements that are linked by a chain of pairs of $R$. The smallest one $E_R$ therefore has as classes the groups of elements linked through the off-diagonal pairs of $R$, and $n(E_R)$ is the sum of the squares of the class sizes. Hence $m(R)=n(E_R)-n(R)$.

$n(E_R)$ depends only on the set $E$ of unordered pairs: $E=\emptyset$ gives classes $1,1,1$ and $n(E_R)=3$; one unordered pair gives classes $2,1$ and $n(E_R)=5$ ($3$ choices of $E$); two or three unordered pairs link all three elements, $n(E_R)=9$ ($4$ choices of $E$).
Mean of $n(E_R)$ over the $64$ relations (each $E$ occurs with $8$ diagonal parts): $\dfrac{1\cdot3+3\cdot5+4\cdot9}{8}=\dfrac{54}{8}=6.75$.

Mean of $n(R)$: each of the $3$ diagonal pairs lies in exactly half of the relations, and each of the $3$ unordered pairs lies in half of them and contributes $2$ ordered pairs. Mean $=3\cdot\frac12+3\cdot2\cdot\frac12=4.5$.
originality_note: New: the 'minimum pairs to add for an equivalence relation' is turned into a statistic averaged over a whole family of relations, split as closure size minus relation size (way 5: counting relations linked with equivalence closure). Closest known: 'R = {(1,2),(2,3)} on {1,2,3}; minimum number of pairs to be added to make R an equivalence relation'. Different because: the quantity must be found for all 64 symmetric relations at once, which needs the classification by linked classes and an averaging split.
blueprint_concepts: Counting reflexive / symmetric / transitive / equivalence relations on a finite set
Minimum number of ordered pairs to make a relation an equivalence relation

concept_use.Counting reflexive / symmetric / transit: The 64 symmetric relations are counted as 2^3 diagonal choices times 2^3 choices of unordered pairs, and the mean is taken over them.
concept_use.Minimum number of ordered pairs to make: m(R) = (size of the smallest equivalence relation containing R) - n(R), with the size from the linked classes (3, 5 or 9).

stem_review: Read as a student: every set, relation and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python by brute-force enumeration, is unique and equals the Answer Plan (positive decimal). Changed: No change.
key_step: Writing m(R) as closure size minus n(R) and classifying the closure by the unordered pairs only.
justification: Two ideas linked (equivalence closure by classes, and counting/averaging over 64 relations) with a numerical answer; each step is standard but the combination is unfamiliar. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q11 (L3) mean over a family.
